Hi Sara / Tom,

Thanks again for the time today — great to learn more about Acme's search use case and the pain points around result quality and freshness. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Recap: you currently have a retrieval candidate pool (BM25 + embeddings) feeding the UI. Re-ranker would sit after retrieval to improve relevance for the top results you surface to users.
- Primary goals you mentioned: improve query relevance for ambiguous queries, reduce obviously wrong top-3 results, and improve satisfaction for long-tail enterprise queries.
- Constraints: low-latency on the first page (target 200-300ms p95 for reranking step if possible), strict PII handling (on-prem eval dataset), and we should avoid major infra changes initially.

Proposed technical next steps:
1) We (Redwood) provide a small integration guide + SDK snippet to run a rerank-only path (send candidates + context -> reranker API). Attachment: redwood-integration-guide.pdf.
2) For evaluation, share a small labeled set (200-500 queries with ground-truth relevance labels) and we run an initial eval (MRR, NDCG@5/10, Precision@1/3). We'll also export a CSV with per-query before/after scores (attached: reranker_eval_results.csv sample).
3) Tuning: start with retrieval top_k=100 (recall-heavy) and reranker return top_k=10 for UI. We'll recommend experiments sweeping reranker_top_k in [5,10,20] and scoring thresholds.
4) Auth & routing: we support API keys for dev, and can route requests to dedicated/private based on your account when you ramp.

Can you share the labeled eval set (or permission to host it temporarily in your VPC) and confirm a preferred time for our SE to join and walk through the SDK? I’ll loop in Vivek (SE) to propose a minimal experiment plan.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Sara / team,

Happy to join Thursday. Quick answers below and a recommended minimal experiment plan: 

Metrics (we typically compute these, but can adapt to your labels):
- MRR@10: mean reciprocal rank considering the first relevant doc position within top 10.
- NDCG@5 and NDCG@10: normalized discounted cumulative gain using graded relevance if you provide multi-grade labels (we accept binary or graded).
- Precision@1 and Precision@3: fraction of relevant docs in the top 1 / top 3.
- Recall@100 (for retrieval recall diagnostics).

If you have a custom schema, send a mapping doc and we’ll compute both your native metric and our standard metrics so you can compare.

Candidate format:
- Preferred: JSONL where each line contains {"query_id":"...","query_text":"...","candidates":[{"id":"doc-123","vector":[...],"score":0.83,"meta":{...},"text":"..."}, ...] }.
- Minimum: id + vector + score + metadata is enough for a reranker if you can’t share full text. For initial offline eval we can accept vectors + IDs (we rehydrate text on our side if given an allowlist), but for on-prem/private eval we can run with only IDs + vectors.

Top_k recommendations and tuning: 
- Retrieval top_k = 100 to start (maximize recall).
- Reranker candidates = 10 (what you show in UI). Run experiments with reranker_top_k in [5,10,20]; often 10 gives a good balance.
- For multi-stage: retrieve 100 -> embed + coarse filter -> rerank top 10. For speed-critical flows we can cache reranker KV outputs for prefix queries to reduce repeated work.

Latency & batching tradeoffs: 
- Dedicated capacity: 200-300ms p95 for reranker-only is achievable on a dedicated 16GB GPU instance with our optimized runtime, assuming batch size 1 (no batching).
- Batching decreases per-token cost but increases latency. If you enable micro-batching (max latency budget 100ms), we can batch small groups (2-8) and still meet 300ms p95 depending on QPS. We’ll recommend a per-route latency SLO and an autoscaling/burst policy.

Auth & SDK:
- Dev: API key (x-api-key header) for quick PoC.
- Prod: support for mTLS or customer-managed KMS-backed tokens for dedicated/private.
- We’ll share a minimal Python SDK snippet (requests + JSONL streaming) for reranker usage and a sample Docker-based harness to run offline eval.

Experiment plan (minimal):
1) You provide 300 labeled queries + candidate exports (JSONL, retrieve top 100).
2) We run baseline (current scores) -> reranker offline eval (MRR,NDCG,P@1/3) and return per-query diffs.
3) Tune reranker_top_k and threshold; run a small A/B on a fraction of traffic if you want live validation.

Attachments: I’ve attached a sample eval CSV and an integration guide.

See you Thursday morning PT; what time works best? I can do 8:30-10:30am PT.

-Vivek
